div.div: رَجُلٌ مُتْلِفٌ لِمَالِهِ , (Msb,) or ↓ رَجُلٌ مِتْلَفٌ , and ↓ مِتْلَافٌ , (M,) A man who destroys, or wastes, his property: (M:) or the last has an intensive signification, (Msb,) meaning who destroys, or wastes, his property much. (S.) You say also, رَجُلٌ مُخْلِفٌ مُتْلِفٌ, (K, and Har p. 312,) or ↓ مِخْلَفٌ مِتْلَفٌ , (TA in art. خلف,) and مِخْلَافٌ, ↓ مِتْلَافٌ , (K, and Har ubi suprà,) meaning A man of courage and liberality, who makes what he takes as spoil, of the property of his enemies, to supply the place of that which he consumes by expenditure to satisfy the claims of his friends. (Har ubi suprà.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
